title: 2016 AMC 12A Problem 5
statement: Goldbach’s conjecture states that every even integer greater than \(2\) can be written as the sum of two prime numbers (for example, \(2016=13+2003\)). So far, no one has been able to prove that the conjecture is true, and no one has found a counterexample to show that the conjecture is false. What would a counterexample consist of?

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text:
an odd integer greater than \(2\) that can be written as the
sum of two prime numbers

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text:
an odd integer greater than \(2\) that cannot be written as the
sum of two prime numbers

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text:
an even integer greater than \(2\) that can be written as the
sum of two numbers that are not prime

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text:
an even integer greater than \(2\) that can be written as the
sum of two prime numbers

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text:
an even integer greater than \(2\) that cannot
be written as the sum of two prime numbers

solutions.text:
A counterexample must satisfy the hypothesis of being an even integer greater than \(2\) while failing the conclusion that it can be written as the sum of two prime numbers.

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: A counterexample keeps the hypothesis but breaks the conclusion
The hypothesis is “even integer greater than \(2\)”; the conclusion is “a sum of two primes”
